content.text:
The flag adds a compatibility shim to the bundle. With `--legacy-imports`, `scripts/build.py:18-20` writes `pkg/_legacy.py` into `dist/tally-<version>/`. That file re-exports `group_totals` as `sum_by` and `parse_amount` as `to_decimal`, which are their pre-1.0 names. Without the flag, the bundle has no such file.

The repo doesn't say whether anyone still depends on those old names. I only grepped for "legacy" and haven't searched for `sum_by` or `to_decimal` usage. The runbook gives no reason for the flag either. Dropping it would be safe only if no downstream users still import the old names, and I can't tell that from here.

If you want to check, search the repo for `sum_by` and `to_decimal`, and look at `git log -S legacy-imports -- RUNBOOK.md` to see when and why it was added. If the flag is dead, remove it from step 4 of the runbook. I'd leave `build.py`'s option in place until you decide to drop the shim entirely.
